units.raw: 1.1.1 "Affiliate" means, with respect to any entity, any other entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with such entity, where "control" means the ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting securities or other ownership interests of such entity, or the power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of such entity.

units.raw: 1.1.2 "Confidential Information" means any and all non-public, proprietary, or confidential information disclosed by or on behalf of a Party or its Affiliates (the "Disclosing Party") to the other Party or its Affiliates (the "Receiving Party"), whether orally, visually, electronically, in writing, or in any other tangible or intangible form, that is designated as "Confidential," "Proprietary," or with a similar legend at the time of disclosure, or that reasonably should be understood to be confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances surrounding its disclosure. units.raw: 2.1 Duty of Care. The Receiving Party shall hold and maintain all Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party in strict confidence and shall exercise at least the same degree of care to safeguard and prevent the unauthorized use, dissemination, or disclosure of such Confidential Information as it exercises to protect its own confidential information of a similar nature, which in no event shall be less than a reasonable standard of care.

units.raw: 2.2 Permitted Use. The Receiving Party shall use the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information solely as necessary to evaluate, pursue, or fulfill the Purpose and for no other purpose whatsoever.
units.after_edits: 2.2 Permitted Use. The Receiving Party shall use the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information solely as necessary to evaluate, pursue, or fulfill the Purpose and for no other purpose whatsoever.

units.raw:
2.3 Permitted Disclosures. The Receiving Party shall not disclose or make available any Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party to any third party, except that the Receiving Party may disclose such Confidential Information to those of its Representatives who have a bona fide need to know such information for the Purpose, provided that:
2.3.1 prior to any such disclosure, the Receiving Party informs each such Representative of the confidential nature of the information;
2.3.2 each such Representative is bound by written confidentiality obligations or professional duties of confidentiality no less protective of the Confidential Information than the terms set forth in this Agreement; and
2.3.3 the Receiving Party shall be wholly responsible and liable to the Disclosing Party for any act or omission of any of its Representatives that would constitute a breach of this Agreement if committed by the Receiving Party directly.

4.1 Legal Process. If the Receiving Party or any of its Representatives is required by applicable law, regulation, subpoena, court order, or the rules of any recognized stock exchange or governmental authority to disclose any Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party, the Receiving Party may make such disclosure to the minimum extent legally required, provided that the Receiving Party shall, to the extent legally permissible:
4.1.1 provide the Disclosing Party with prompt prior written notice of such requirement so that the Disclosing Party may seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy; and
4.1.2 reasonably cooperate with the Disclosing Party, at the Disclosing Party's sole expense, in any lawful effort by the Disclosing Party to contest, limit, or obtain confidential treatment for such required disclosure.

units.raw: 5.1 Procedure upon Request. Upon the termination or expiration of this Agreement, or at any time upon the Disclosing Party's written request, the Receiving Party shall within ten (10) business days either promptly return to the Disclosing Party all tangible materials embodying the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information or permanently destroy and erase all such materials (including all copies, extracts, and summaries thereof) in its possession or under its control, and upon request shall provide written certification of such destruction signed by an authorized representative.

Notwithstanding the expiration or earlier termination of this Agreement, the Receiving Party's obligations of confidentiality and non-use with respect to Confidential Information disclosed prior to such expiration or termination shall survive for a fixed period of thirty-six (36) months following the effective date of such expiration or termination; provided, however, that with respect to any item of Confidential Information that rises to the level of a trade secret under applicable law, the restrictions on disclosure and use set forth herein shall not expire at the end of such thirty-six (36) month period but shall instead continue in perpetuity for so long as such information retains its legal status as a protected trade secret.
